title: Fast and High-Resolution Imaging of Pollinated Stigmatic Cells by Tabletop Scanning Electron Microscopy
author: Lucie Riglet
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Materials and reagents Biological materials Arabidopsis thaliana , ecotype Columbia Col-0 plants with flowers at stages 12–15 [4] in individual pots Other materials Straight fine tweezers (Dumont, model: Inox 8) Double-sided black tape (Synergie4, model: DEN-77816) Wood sticks and soft plant ties to stack the plants Sewing thread to tag the emasculated pistils

steps.title: Grow Arabidopsis plants under controlled conditions
steps.instruction: Sow a few Arabidopsis thaliana Col‑0 seeds in 0.25 L plastic pots containing peat‑based compost mixed with 60 kg m⁻³ clay. After one week thin to one plant per pot. Grow plants in a chamber with long‑day cycle (16 h light at 120–150 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, 8 h dark) at 21 °C (day) / 19 °C (night) and ~60 % relative humidity. Water throughout the life cycle, avoiding over‑watering of young plants. Add fertilizer (N/P/K = 18/10/18) to the watering water at 4 mL L⁻¹ once per week. Plants are ready for emasculation four weeks after germination; use only robust stems (3–4 per plant) and avoid older, fragile plants.

steps.title: Water plants thoroughly before emasculation
steps.instruction: On the day before emasculation, water each plant thoroughly to ensure turgid stigmas and pollen.

steps.title: Emasculate stage‑12 buds and label pistils
steps.instruction: Under a stereomicroscope, position the plant in its pot, bend the inflorescences and gently clamp a stage‑12 flower bud between thumb and forefinger. Using straight fine tweezers (Dumont, model Inox 8), remove any older buds, then carefully open the selected bud to expose the stigma. Verify that anthers are not dehiscent; perform emasculation in the morning when anthers are least dehiscent. Cut away anthers (pale yellow), petals and sepals with the tweezers, leaving a small portion of tissue to reduce dehydration. Ensure no pollen grains remain on the stigma papillae; discard the bud if pollen is present. Limit emasculation to ≤5 buds per plant. Attach a sewing thread at the base of each bare pistil for labeling.

steps.title: Stake plants to prevent pollen contact
steps.instruction: Support each plant with wood sticks and soft plant ties (as shown in Fig. 2F) to keep the bare pistils away from other flowers. Return the plants to the culture room. If imaging stage‑13 stigmas, wait approximately 18 h after emasculation before pollination.

steps.title: Pollinate emasculated stigmas with fresh pollen
steps.instruction: Collect a single dehiscent anther from a non‑emasculated flower at stage 13–early 14 using the fine tweezers. Gently brush the anther onto a tissue to remove excess pollen, then lightly brush the pollen onto the emasculated stigma, depositing only a small amount of grains. Perform pollination at room temperature (~20 °C) with ≥50 % relative humidity to promote optimal pollen germination.

steps.title: Incubate post‑pollination for desired imaging time
steps.instruction: Leave the pollinated plants on the bench at room temperature (~22 °C). For imaging pollen hydration, wait 10–15 min; for imaging longer pollen tubes, wait 30–60 min before sample preparation.

steps.title: Transversely cut pistils for SEM sampling
steps.instruction: At the designated time post‑pollination, use fine tweezers to cut each pistil transversely in the middle of the ovary (Fig. 4). Ensure the resulting sample height does not exceed 0.5 cm so it fits into the SEM chamber.

steps.title: Mount cut pistils on double‑sided tape
steps.instruction: Place 2–3 cut pistils vertically onto a 4 × 2 cm piece of double‑sided black tape (Synergie4, model DEN‑77816) that is affixed to the SEM platform. Keep pistils at least 1 cm apart to avoid overlap.

steps.title: Configure tabletop SEM parameters
steps.instruction: Insert the platform into the Hirox SEM SH‑3000 and seal the door. Set the chamber temperature to –20 °C and wait until it stabilises. Select an accelerating voltage of 15 kV and turn on the vacuum.

steps.title: Image samples promptly and acquire photographs
steps.instruction: Observe each sample within the first 15 min to avoid cell collapse. For rapid screening, use the AutoFocus function. Zoom in at high magnification on central pollen grains to adjust focus, contrast and brightness, then zoom out to capture a broader view of the pistil. Acquire images of the stigma surface, pollen hydration state, and pollen tube paths as required.
